justifications.functional_suitability: Cataloging physical and digital items is supported by Catalog Management Component, Core Domain Service, and the Digital Content Provider integration. Circulation and self-service requirements are comprehensively satisfied by Circulation & Lending Engine, Web Application, and Self-Service Kiosk App.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The sub-800ms search requirement (R-05) is addressed via the dedicated Search Service with Elasticsearch, Catalog L2 Cache Component in Redis, Search & Filter Controller debouncing, and PgBouncer connection pooling.
justifications.compatibility: External integration is well established: Identity Provider via OIDC, Payment Gateway and Notification Service via REST, National Library Registry via Registry Sync Handler, and local hardware via Kiosk Host Bridge (OPOS/UPOS).
justifications.usability: Both target personas are accommodated: Library Patron is provided a responsive Web Application and touch-optimized Self-Service Kiosk App, while Librarian has full circulation and cataloging capabilities via Web Application.
justifications.reliability: Reliability and fault tolerance are ensured by Search Circuit Breaker, Offline Queue Manager for disconnected kiosk sessions, read replicas in Database, and Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) Managers in Kafka and Async Worker.
justifications.security: The EU data residency constraint is directly enforced by Geo-Filtering & Compliance Module and EU Data Residency Enforcer. Identity verification, access controls, and transport security are maintained by Authentication & Authorization Filter and TLS termination.
justifications.maintainability: High maintainability is achieved through clear domain segregation (Core Domain Service, Search Service, Reporting & Analytics Service), loosely coupled event flows using Notification & Event Bus, and contract enforcement via Schema Registry.
justifications.portability: Microservices and backing technologies (Spring Boot, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, MinIO S3) are container-friendly and portable across standard EU cloud hosting providers without proprietary vendor lock-in.

PERF-01.justification: Dedicated Elasticsearch Search Service with pre-serialized facets in Redis L2 cache and API Gateway load balancing support low-latency search. Passing all searches through Core Domain Service introduces a slight serialization hop under extreme concurrency.
sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch cluster sizing and replica count
Redis L2 cache hit ratio for catalogue queries
tradeoffs: Routing search via Core Domain Service adds minor latency versus direct API Gateway routing

PERF-02.justification: Catalogue modifications are decoupled from search queries via Kafka event publishing and an asynchronous Index Synchronizer Consumer in the Search Service. Updates index well within 5 minutes without degrading the read path.
sensitivity_points: Kafka consumer lag on indexing topics during bulk cataloguing
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency in search index in exchange for isolated write and search throughput

AVAIL-01.justification: Search Service includes Resilience4j circuit breaking to isolate search failures. Circulation operations depend strictly on PostgreSQL and Redis within the Core Domain Service, safeguarding active loan transactions against search cluster degradation.
sensitivity_points: Circuit breaker trip thresholds and fallback policies
Elasticsearch multi-node clustering and automatic failover
tradeoffs: Graceful degradation disables search while preserving critical circulation and loan transactions

AVAIL-02.justification: Stateless React Web App and multi-instance Kiosks route through API Gateway with load balancing and upstream circuit breaking. Kiosks also incorporate an Offline Queue Manager to buffer transactions during local or network failures.
sensitivity_points: Gateway upstream health check frequency and timeout intervals
tradeoffs: Local queueing allows autonomous operation but requires eventual synchronization upon reconnect

MOD-01.justification: Digital Content Provider is defined at context level but absent from container bindings. Ingestion relies on generic Catalog Management and Async Worker components without a modular provider SPI or dedicated connector.
sensitivity_points: Abstraction level of digital content ingestion interfaces
Extensibility of schema and worker tasks
tradeoffs: Centralizing ingestion in domain services simplifies design but increases modification footprint

MOD-02.justification: Circulation rules are encapsulated directly within the Spring Boot Circulation & Lending Engine. The architecture lacks a dynamic rules engine, external policy engine, or configuration management mechanism to adapt rules at runtime without redeployment.
sensitivity_points: Hardcoded rule branching versus dynamic rule evaluation
Configuration reload capabilities in Spring Boot services
tradeoffs: Compile-time business logic ensures type safety but sacrifices operational agility

SEC-01.justification: Data residency is strictly reinforced across tiers: Geo-Filtering in API Gateway, node pinning in Elasticsearch, Row-Level Security EU Residency Enforcer in PostgreSQL, and explicit regional logging and storage endpoints.
sensitivity_points: Correctness of geo-IP classification tables at API Gateway
Row-level security enforcement across all database schemas
tradeoffs: Rigid regional filtering may block valid international patrons traveling outside the EU

SEC-02.justification: API Gateway enforces stateless JWT authentication while Patron Account Manager validates authorization boundaries. Unauthorized requests are denied, exceptions report through telemetry, and audit events persist into the dedicated Audit & Reporting Schema.
sensitivity_points: Token subject and patron ID correlation verification in domain logic
Immutability of audit logs in PostgreSQL
tradeoffs: Granular identity validation on every query incurs slight compute and logging overhead
